\begin{abstract}
We give a self-contained finite-block theorem for four-dimensional $\SUtwo$
heat-kernel lattice gauge theory.  On the side-two cubical block, rooted
spanning-tree gauge removes the nonconstant gauge orbit with exact product-Haar
accounting.  The reduced block has $136$ scalar link coordinates.  Seventeen
independent boundary-face curvature sums are retained, leaving a
$119$-dimensional scalar fiber; with three color components the retained and
fiber dimensions are $51$ and $357$.  Exact rational elimination and an
$LDL^{\mathsf T}$ certificate prove a cotree curvature floor $1/25$.
Quaternion product--log estimates and an analytic $\SUtwo$ heat-kernel image
bound then control the exact nonlinear plaquette action on an explicit local
cylinder.  For link radius $10^{-5}$ and $0<t\le10^{-18}$, the scaled action
Hessian differs from its tangent quadratic form by less than $1/400$.
Consequently every conditional fiber density is uniformly strongly
log-concave with curvature at least $3/(80t)$, its Wasserstein response to the
retained coordinate is at most $1/3$, and exact fiber integration produces an
effective retained Hessian within $1/15$ of the identity.  Two independent
standard-library verifiers certify all topology, rank, spectral, and rational
budget claims.  The result is a restricted one-block certificate: it neither
controls the interacting measure outside the cylinder nor establishes
repeated renormalization, a continuum theory, or a physical mass gap.
\end{abstract}
